CSVProcessor.read_csv:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Reads a CSV file, uses the first row as the title, collects all remaining rows into a list, and returns the title and data rows." read_csv]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> file_name </REF>: string "Path or file identifier of the CSV file to read."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> return_value </REF>: tuple "A tuple whose first element is title, the first CSV row, and whose second element is data, the list of remaining CSV rows."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize an empty list named data. RESULT data]
            [COMMAND Open file_name in read text mode ('r') within a with block and bind it to file. RESULT file]
            [COMMAND Within the with block, create a csv.reader object from file. RESULT reader]
            [COMMAND Within the with block, get the next row from reader and assign it to title; if reader has no rows, a StopIteration exception propagates. RESULT title]
            [COMMAND Within the with block, for each remaining row in reader, append row to data. RESULT data]
            [COMMAND After the with block, return the tuple (title, data). RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
CSVProcessor.write_csv:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Writes the provided rows of data to a CSV file and returns 1 on success or 0 if any exception occurs." write_csv]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> data </REF>: Iterable[Iterable[str]] "Rows of data to write to the CSV file."
        <REF> file_name </REF>: str "Path or name of the file to open for writing."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> status </REF>: int "Returns 1 if the CSV is written successfully, otherwise returns 0."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Within a with block that ensures the file is closed after the operation, open file_name for writing with newline='' and assign the file object to file. RESULT file]
            [COMMAND Within the with block for file, create a csv.writer object using file and assign it to writer. RESULT writer]
            [COMMAND Within the with block for file, write all rows from data to the CSV file using writer.writerows(data). RESULT writerows_result]
            [COMMAND Return integer 1. RESULT status]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: Any exception occurs while opening the file, creating the CSV writer, or writing rows.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return integer 0. RESULT status]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
CSVProcessor.process_csv_data:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Reads a CSV file, extracts and uppercases a specified column, and writes the transformed data to a new processed CSV file." process_csv_data]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> N </REF>: integer "Column index used to extract a value from each row in the CSV data."
        <REF> save_file_name </REF>: string "Name of the input CSV file; its base name before the first dot is used to build the output file name."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> return_value </REF>: any "Return value from self.write_csv after writing the processed CSV data."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call self.read_csv with save_file_name and destructure the returned value into title and data. RESULT title, data]
            [COMMAND For each row in data, extract the element at index N using a list comprehension, and assign the resulting list to column_data. RESULT column_data]
            [COMMAND Uppercase each element in column_data using a list comprehension and reassign the resulting list to column_data. RESULT column_data]
            [COMMAND Create new_data as a two-element list containing title as the first element and the uppercased column_data as the second element. RESULT new_data]
            [COMMAND Derive the output file name by splitting save_file_name on '.' and taking the first segment, then appending '_process.csv'. RESULT output_file_name]
            [COMMAND Return the result of calling self.write_csv with new_data and the derived output file name. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
